title: Playing Carnival balls today and the slow season
summary: He played eighteen balls last year, the season used to be longer, and he turns away low-paying club dates.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Yeah, pretty good. You know, 18. So from January 1 up at the Carnival I played 18 balls. And that's not counting the gigs in the middle. But I love it. You see, because I know, it used to be, although this year I didn't play, I played like Friday, Saturday, Sunday, Monday, off Tuesday, and played Wednesday, no, off Tuesday, Wednesday, and played Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday, Monday. But I've seen the time where we had the whole thing. We played Friday, Saturday, Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday, Monday. And that's where I won't get it back. It's tiresome. But the only thing you do is think about the little money.
You probably, I'm sure it's like most people, you're making hay while the sun shines. Right. The Mardi Gras.
You know what I'm talking about right now? You know how many gigs I've had since Mardi Gras? Two. Two.

I've had two. That's all. And I'm off this weekend. I was off last week. I'm off. Well, we're going to play this thing next Sunday, my brother, for a dough. I'm probably going to make a quarter. But it really don't matter. But I'm doing this because he want to do it, not because I want. If I ever left up to me, I wouldn't play this. I feel like in my years in this business, I have already played that kind of stuff. So I paid my dues that way.
